NutriCore Foods - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriCore Foods Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one on your touchtone phone. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Vice President of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriCore Foods's Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are Sarah Jenkins, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and David Kim, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins.

Sarah Jenkins (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2023. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: Performance of key brands and product categories, Impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, Market share trends for major brands, Key achievements and challenges in the quarter, Overall company performance highlights, Revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, and Performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience.

First, regarding Performance of key brands and product categories: Our Consumer Brands segment, which accounts for 72% of total net sales, achieved organic growth of 7.2% year-over-year, surpassing the industry average of 4.1% according to NielsenIQ. This growth stemmed from 4.5% volume increases and 2.7% from price and mix improvements, even as we managed input cost inflation in commodities such as cocoa, sugar, and dairy through precise pricing strategies and supply chain optimizations that boosted gross margins by 150 basis points to 38.4%.

Our leading snack brand, CrunchMax—our savory snacks powerhouse similar to PepsiCo's Lay's or Frito-Lay—generated net sales of $1.2 billion, up 12.3% organically. Volumes rose 8.2%, propelled by the rollout of air-fried variants with 40% less sodium, gaining 2.1 share points in the U.S. salty snacks category based on IRI data. Premium trends are strong, with high-protein and baked options now comprising 28% of the portfolio, up from 18% last year, and EBITDA margins widening 220 basis points to 24.7% thanks to streamlined production at our new Reno, Nevada facility. In APAC, CrunchMax sales jumped 18% via e-commerce tie-ups with Shopee and Lazada in Southeast Asia.

Turning to beverages, the VitaQuench hydration and functional drinks lineup—positioned against Gatorade and Prime—reached $850 million in net sales, flat organically amid a strategic portfolio shift. Core sports drinks fell 3.1% due to reduced at-home consumption post-COVID, but zero-sugar, electrolyte-infused ready-to-drink lines exploded 25%, now 35% of the segment. Our proprietary HydroBoost formula, using plant-based electrolytes from seaweed, cut sugar by 50% and lifted repeat purchases 14% in panels. North America volumes were steady at +1%, while EMEA grew 2% despite 9% inflation-driven downtrading. We're investing $50 million in aseptic filling technology at our Monterrey, Mexico plant to fuel LATAM growth.

In Health & Wellness, PureVeg plant-based dairy alternatives—drawing inspiration from Oatly and Chobani—surged 22.4% to $650 million. Almond and oat milks fueled 15% volume gains, seizing 4.2 share points in the U.S. non-dairy milk category amid 12% expansion per SPINS. Margins dipped slightly to 32.1% from almond supply issues, but hedging, vertical integration, and a new 100,000-acre regenerative farm in California's Central Valley promise 300 basis points of accretion in FY24. APAC led with 31% organic growth from premium RTD protein shakes in 7-Eleven and FamilyMart.

Convenience foods via QuickBite Meals—microwaveable bowls and frozen entrees like Amy's Kitchen—grew 9.8% organically to $500 million. Foodservice traffic rebounded 11% through limited-service restaurant partnerships like Subway's premium wraps with our sous-vide proteins. We countered private label pressure with 18 new 'Clean Label' SKUs using no preservatives and upcycled ingredients like spent grain from breweries.

By region, North America drove 58% of segment sales with 8.5% growth, strong in Walmart and Kroger. EMEA grew 3.2% despite energy volatility, aided by UK reduced-plastic packaging that improved brand perception 17 points per Kantar. APAC and LATAM excelled at 14.6% and 11.2%, aligning with Nielsen's 9% emerging market category growth from urbanization and premium on-the-go demand.

These outcomes embody our 'Taste the Future' strategy: 25% of R&D to functional nutrition targeting Gen Z's $400 billion spend, 90% recyclable packaging by year-end per EU PPWR, and 12% Scope 3 emissions cuts via supplier audits. Our AI-powered NutriCore Network slashed inventory days 15% and hit 98% on-time delivery despite port issues.

Second, concerning Impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: Operating in over 180 markets with 65% of our $15.2 billion Q3 net revenues from international operations outside North America, we're exposed to FX volatility, especially with the U.S. dollar strengthening 8% year-to-date against key currencies. Reported revenues rose 6% year-over-year, but on a constant currency basis excluding FX, growth was a solid 11%, with 4% from organic volume/mix and 1% from pricing. FX created a 5 percentage point drag, equating to about $760 million in foregone revenue, aligning with trends since Q1.

Regionally, Europe (28% of revenue) saw the euro weaken 6% quarter-over-quarter, a $350 million headwind. Our Aquafina-like premium waters and Gatorade-style hydration grew 3% CC on summer demand in Western Europe, but translation hit hard in Germany and France (40% of regional sales) for zero-sugar production. The pound's 4% drop added $120 million pressure on snack lines like Lay's kettle chips, up 6% CC from premiumization.

Asia-Pacific (18%) endured 12% currency depreciation in yuan, rupee, and Aussie dollar, a $275 million hit. China CC revenues for Lipton-like teas and RTD coffees rose 7% on millennial e-commerce via Tmall, though yuan weakness obscured it like at Coca-Cola. Australia and Japan benefited from local sugarcane hedges for Fanta flavors.

Latin America and emerging markets (19%) faced Brazilian real -11%, peso -9%, and Argentine volatility, $230 million impact. CC growth hit 8% from Propel fitness waters and snacking, with inflation pricing offsetting cocoa/sugar via 70% local corn procurement, akin to Mondelez.

North America (35%) grew 4% CC on Pepsi and Doritos resilience.

Mitigations include a hedging program covering 70-80% of 12-month exposures with forwards and collars, booking $165 million gains in Q3. Extending to 18 months for EM currencies, like Unilever. Natural hedges: 85% local COGS (barley in Europe, palm oil in Indonesia). Pricing tests yielded 2-4% hikes in 15 markets without volume loss, per Diageo model. Diversifying to stable CAD/SGD, $2 billion Southeast Asia bottling investment.

For Q4/FY24, expect 5-7 ppt FX headwind if USD persists; CC guide 4-6% organic with plant-based Doritos and Pepsi Zero launches. Balance sheet with $8 billion cash handles 10% USD rally stress.

Third, in terms of Market share trends for major brands: Drawing from Nielsen, IRI, and internal ACV data through Q3, in the $7.5 trillion global F&B market with our focus areas at 2.8% YoY volume growth amid inflation and health shifts, we hold 12.4% in non-alcs (+40 bps) and 9.8% in savory snacks (+110 bps).

In non-alcoholic beverages (category +1.9% volume), CSDs see Coke Classic/Diet at 43.2% U.S. share (-120 bps) from health erosion and Ozempic. Pepsi/Mountain Dew at 24.7% flat, via 7-Eleven/Circle K velocity. Energy drinks fragment: Red Bull 38.5% global (-250 bps), Monster 31.2% (+380 bps) on Ultra zero-sugar and Reign/NOS. Celsius 7.8% (+450 bps) on TikTok DTC. Our SparkVita at 4.2% (+90 bps) via 10-calorie plant-caffeine, 88% grocery ACV, 15% e-comm Amazon.

Sparkling waters/RTD teas (+5.4%): LaCroix 22.4% (-180 bps), Pepsi Bubly 18.9% (+240 bps) on influencers/Charli D'Amelio/recyclable cans -30% waste. Our ZenLeaf RTD teas 6.7% (+70 bps) vs Lipton 14.2% (-50 bps), matcha line 15% millennial penetration.

North America blended 11.8% stable. EMEA: Coke CSD 39% (-200 bps) from HFSS bans, SparkVita +150 bps to 3.9% EU certs. APAC +4.2% volumes, Wang Lao Ji 28%, our Tingyi JV to 2.1% (+80 bps) mango-ginger Tmall. LatAm volatile, Gatorade 26% (-100 bps) to our rehydrants soccer ties.

Savory snacks ($250B +3.1%): Frito-Lay 32.6% U.S. flat, Flamin' Hot innovations 1.2x velocity. Mondelez Ritz 11.4% (+60 bps) hybrids. Pringles 8.7% (-40 bps). Our CrunchBar 7.2% (+130 bps), air-pop -25% oil, DoorDash.

Strategies: Divest 5% sugary SKUs, $150M to BFY R&D for 20% plant-snack share FY25. E-comm 18% sales (+6pts), Amazon 92% ACV. Sustainability: recycled PET, regen ag +12 NPS Europe 65% ESG priority Kantar. Dynamic Walmart pricing holds 42% margins despite 4% cocoa/alum inflation.

Expect 100-150 bps FY24 accretion, $300M pipeline AI flavors, Prime challenger.

Fourth, looking at Key achievements and challenges in the quarter: We posted net revenues of $1.28 billion for the segment in focus, up 7.2% reported or 5.1% organic excluding FX and Canada soup divestiture. Adjusted EPS $0.92, +4 cents beat from pricing/productivity over inflation.

Achievements: Volumes +4.8% beverages led by VitaQuench +22%, share in $12B enhanced water vs Gatorade/BodyArmor. NutriOat oat milk to 15% NA share (+4pts), Kroger exclusives 35% Amazon/Instacart. High-protein bars +12% Kind/RXBAR style. NA 62% rev +9.5% ACV 85% Walmart/Whole Foods. APAC +14% BrewBoost RTD coffee Indonesia/Vietnam $8B market +28%. EMEA +3% UK health bars +2pts vs Mondelez.

Supply chain: AI forecasting 70% NA plants, inventory -18%, availability 96%. 45% regen cocoa West Africa, DJSI nod. Pricing +6.2%, elasticity -2.5. Gross margins +210bps 38.4%, dairy -11% QoQ hedges, Mexico aseptic -15% costs.

Challenges: Commodities—sugar +22% El Niño Brazil, cocoa $4200/ton +150%, chocolate margins -180bps, dairy +8%. Hedged 65% FY24. Premium slowdown EMEA flat at-home energy crisis UK trade-down. Foodservice +2% vs 8% avg, Starbucks/McD traffic recession. APAC freight +12 days Red Sea +$0.02/unit tea. Coke/Unilever promos premium mix to 58%. LatAm +1% Argentina 35% inflation Mexico HFSS delays.

Playbook: Prune juices $150M divest, $120M R&D precision fermentation 20% rev new <3yrs. FreshTrace blockchain Q1'24 transparency SEC climate.

Fifth, reviewing Overall company performance highlights: This marked our strongest Q3 in a decade across beverages, snacks, nutrition. Net revenues $15.2 billion, +8% reported, 6% organic (volume +2%, pricing +3%, mix +1%), 11th straight organic quarter vs industry 2-3% Nielsen/IRI. CC nearer 9% sans FX EM.

Beverages (FrostQuench sodas, VitaGlow waters, energy like Celsius/Prime) +7% organic $8.1B, +110bps U.S. non-alc RTD Circana, low/no-sugar 45% vol (+7pts). Snacks/Nutrition (CrunchMax, NutriBar) +5% $5.4B, double-digit plant-protein offset salty private label. Int'l Foods $1.7B +4%, SKU rationalization +15% efficiency.

Adjusted op income +12% $3.8B, margins +140bps 25.1%. EBITDA +14% $3.5B, gross +220bps 38.2% from 5-7% pricing, $450M YTD Zero Loss AI/robotic 25 plants, dairy/wheat mid-single vs 20%+ FY22, $120M palm/cocoa hedges vs Hershey peers 40% cocoa surge.

EPS $1.85 +12% reported +15% core, asset-light 60% high-margin convenience.

Regions: NA 65% +9% e-comm 18% Amazon/DoorDash, Costco +25% multipacks. LatAm +12% CC Brazil/Mexico FrostQuench +2pts soccer. Europe +2% offset HFSS/plastic taxes premium hydration +8%. APAC +10% China +15% RTD tea India NutriBar +30% Blinkit.

Cash flow $4.1B YTD +18%, $1.2B dividends, $800M buybacks $5B auth, net leverage 2.1x. VegaPlant $1.1B acq $300M synergies.

Pillars: Premium/health 20 new low-sugar Q4 $50B BFY 12% CAGR Euromonitor; recycled PET 65% bev; blockchain 80% cocoa/palm -12% waste top MSCI.

Raised FY23: organic 5-6%, EPS $6.95-7.05 (+10% mid), op margin +100-150bps. Hedging/diversification vs FX/commodities.

Sixth, analyzing Revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance: Entering 2023 cautiously on cocoa/coffee/dairy inflation and soft at-home, initial guide organic sales 3-5%, adj EPS $4.85-5.05, EBITDA margins +50-100bps 15.5-16.0%, mid-single pricing/volume/gross expansion.

Raising today on Q2 strength/back-half momentum: Organic sales 5-7% (pricing 4.5-5.5% EDLP beverages/snacks, volume/mix 0.5-1.5%, VitalQuench adaptogen +25% tests). EPS $5.15-5.35 (+8-12% vs 2023 $4.78). EBITDA +160-210bps 16.6-17.1%, gross 39.0-39.5% (Q2 +200bps). FCF $1.2-1.4B, inventory -8% SAP S/4HANA +15% forecast 45 plants.

Segments: Beverages 55% 7-9% HarvestSpark CSD/Pure Leaf RTD, 6% pricing HFCS +12%, vol +1.5% zero-sugar Coke style. Snacks 35% 4-6% NutriCrunch +18% Q2 RTD health.

Regions: NA 60% 6-8% Costco/Sam's +12%. EMEA 20% flat-2% dairy +8% sugar tax, plant pivot 5% pricing. APAC/LatAm 20% 8-10% Shopee/Mercado +30% probiotic yogurt Danone-like.

Pillars: Supply resilience 70% cocoa $4200 hedges $150M H1 savings Mondelez-style. Premium/innovation 40% R&D functional $50B 9% CAGR Nielsen. Digital/ESG AI -20% stockouts regen 500 farmers Scope3 -15% net-zero pkg 2030.

Risks: FX hedge 80%, El Niño coffee, private label +2pts IRI. Q2 45% gross pricing power. Long-term 7-10% sales CAGR 10%+ EPS, 3-4% CapEx, 28th div hike +8%.

Seventh, examining Performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience: Channels grew 7.2% consolidated, 4.8% organic (vol +3.1%, pricing +1.5%, mix +0.2%). Penetration +1.8pts 68% NA IRI/Nielsen, velocity +2.4%, +110bps $128B bev/snack share vs 2.9% cat.

Retail (58%) +5.1% organic vol +2.7% pricing +2.4%. Grocery +6.2% PowerAde/PlantPower 15% ACV 6mo vs Pepsi Rockstar. Mass +3.8% Walmart/Target +12% linear Zero Sugar +4.1% Circana share. Club +1.2% lapping Omicron, co-mfg BJ's margins 28.4% +90bps. NA +6.4% e-comm +18%. EMEA +2.1% UK/Ger inflation trade-down HealthFirst -30% sugar +7% loyalty France Kantar. APAC India/China +9.2%. AI planograms Kroger +11% sell-thru, mid-single FY24 +200bps share functional tailwinds.

Foodservice (24%) +10.3% vol +5.6% pricing +4.5%. QSR +13.1% NPD 95% pre-COVID McD Fiery Splash +$28M Starbucks RTD 4200 doors. Casual +7.4% Sysco/US Foods portion snack pouches Applebee's/Chili's +22% cases. Midwest labor +8%, EMEA +11% inflation delistings UK. LatAm +14.2% Brazil QSR Giraffas/Bob's juices. OperatorSync 85% top-50 chains -18% stockouts -12% waste margins +220bps 26.1%, FY24 12-15% travel normalize.

Convenience (18%) +14.7% vol +7.9% pricing +6.4%. C-stores +16.2% 7-Eleven/Circle K Grab-N-Go +25% vel 92% ACV Nielsen (+11pts). Gas/travel +12.8% Buc-ee's jerky +$15M. Vending +11.4%. US +15.9% PM fuel. APAC +22.1% Alfamart pouches. EMEA +9.3% sugar tax. ImpulseMax roller-grill 8500 doors +30% basket, recyclable +14 NPS margins 32.2% +150bps.

Mix +50bps high-margin conv/foodservice EBITDA 22.4% +110bps. Inflation 4-6% cocoa/alum hedge 85% Q1 Mexico co-pack $12M save. Right-the-Shelf RFID 95% exec Mondelez. 15 SKUs low-cal plant $45B functional, $150M APAC capex. Reaffirm FY organic 6-8% margins +100-150bps.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah outlined comprehensively, we achieved solid results in Q3 2023. Net sales were $15.2 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.2%, impacted positively by productivity gains and pricing discipline despite commodity volatility. Operating income was $3.8 billion, and earnings per share were $1.85. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $8 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are raising our guidance for organic revenue growth to 5-6% and adjusted EPS to $6.95-$7.05.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Doe (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Sarah Jenkins (CEO):
Thanks, John. Inflation in commodities like sugar up 22% from El Niño, cocoa at record $4,200 per ton up 150%, and dairy 8% over plan have pressured margins, particularly in chocolate by 180 basis points and overall input costs. We've countered with 6.2% targeted pricing across the portfolio—elasticity at -2.5 reflecting brand loyalty—65-80% hedging coverage, local sourcing for 85% international COGS, and productivity like $450 million YTD from AI and robotics, delivering 210-220 basis point gross margin expansion to 38.2-38.4%. This positions us resiliently as costs ease.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Jane Smith (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for new product and what is the expected impact of product?

Lisa Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Jane. Our new VitaQuench zero-sugar RTD line with HydroBoost plant electrolytes is ramping aggressively, building on 25% growth in test markets. Plans include $50 million capacity at Monterrey for LATAM/APAC, 88% ACV grocery plus 15% e-comm via Amazon, and 18 new SKUs in clean label extensions. Expect 20%+ revenue contribution to beverages in FY24, 1-2 share points in functional hydration akin to Celsius gains, and 200-300 bps margin lift from premium mix now 35-45% segment, targeting $50 billion BFY market at 9-12% CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Johnson with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Bob Johnson (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Kim (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, Bob. Disruptions like Red Sea reroutings adding 12 days freight from APAC and port issues are met with our NutriCore Network AI forecasting across 70% plants, cutting inventory 15-18%, stockouts 20%, waste 12%, hitting 96-98% availability/OTD. Local sourcing 85% COGS, regen programs 45% cocoa/500 farmers stabilizing almonds/dairy, blockchain FreshTrace 80-100% transparency for recalls/ESG. OperatorSync for foodservice and RFID shelves ensure 95% execution, plus Mexico/Reno expansions saving 15% conversion, hedging 70% commodities.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Alice Lee with Barclays. Please proceed.

Alice Lee (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Michael Chen (CFO):
Alice, Q4 outlook builds on Q3 momentum with CC organic 4-6%, despite 5-7 ppt FX headwind. Channels like convenience/foodservice 12-15% growth, retail mid-single. Margins +100-150 bps from productivity/$150-450M savings, pricing 4.5-5.5%. Raised FY organic 5-7%, EPS $5.15-5.35 core, EBITDA 16.6-17.1%. Risks FX/commodities hedged 80%, but balance sheet firepower for M&A/returns supports 7-10% long-term CAGR.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Sarah Jenkins for closing remarks.

Sarah Jenkins (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriCore Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
